title.zh: 卷一百三十六 僭偽列傳三: 王建 孟知祥
title.en: Volume 136: Biographies of Usurpers 3 - Wang Jian, Meng Zhixiang
title.raw: 卷一百三十六 僭偽列傳三: 王建 孟知祥 Volume 136: Biographies of Usurpers 3 - Wang Jian, Meng Zhixiang

sentences.zh: 王建，陳州項城人。

translations.literal: Wang Jian was a native of Xiangcheng in Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian came from Xiangcheng in Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 唐末，隸名於忠武軍。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tang, his name was enrolled in the Zhongwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of the Tang, he was mustered into the Zhongwu Army.

sentences.zh: 秦宗權據蔡州，懸重賞以募之，建始自行間得補軍候。

translations.literal: Qin Zongquan held Cai Prefecture and offered heavy rewards to recruit men; Jian at first came forward on his own from the ranks and was appointed military scout.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Zongquan seized Cai Prefecture and posted lavish bounties to raise troops, Jian stepped forward from the ranks on his own and was made a military scout.

sentences.zh: 廣明中，黃巢陷長安，僖宗幸蜀。

translations.literal: In the Guangming era, Huang Chao took Chang'an, and Emperor Xizong went to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangming reign period, Huang Chao captured Chang'an and Emperor Xizong fled to Shu.

sentences.zh: 時梁祖為巢將，領眾攻襄、鄧，宗權遣小校鹿晏宏從監軍楊復光率師攻之，建亦預行。

translations.literal: At that time the Liang founder was a general under Chao, leading troops to attack Xiang and Deng; Zongquan sent the junior officer Lu Yanhong to follow the supervising commissioner Yang Fuguang in leading an army against him, and Jian also took part in the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the future Liang founder served Huang Chao as a general and marched on Xiang and Deng; Zongquan sent the junior officer Lu Yanhong under the supervising commissioner Yang Fuguang to oppose him, and Jian marched with them.

sentences.zh: 是歲，復光入援京師，明年破賊收京城。

translations.literal: That year Fuguang entered the capital region to relieve the court; the next year he defeated the rebels and recovered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That year Fuguang marched to relieve the capital; the following year he broke the rebels and retook the city.

sentences.zh: 初，復光以忠武軍八千人立為八都，晏宏與建各一都校也。

translations.literal: Initially Fuguang organized the eight thousand men of the Zhongwu Army into eight commands; Yanhong and Jian each commanded one command.
translations.idiomatic: At first Fuguang divided the Zhongwu Army's eight thousand men into eight commands, with Yanhong and Jian each leading one.

sentences.zh: 復光死，晏弘率八都迎扈行在，至山南，乃攻剽金、商諸郡縣，得兵數萬，進逼興元，節度使牛叢棄城而去，晏宏因自為留後，建等為屬郡刺史，不令之任。

translations.literal: After Fuguang died, Yanhong led the eight commands to escort the traveling court; reaching Shannan, he then raided the prefectures and counties of Jin and Shang, gathered tens of thousands of troops, and pressed on Xingyuan; the military governor Niu Cong abandoned the city and fled; Yanhong thereupon made himself acting governor, while Jian and the others were named prefects of subordinate prefectures but were not allowed to take office.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuguang died, Yanhong led the eight commands to join the court on the move. Reaching Shannan, he plundered Jin and Shang and their districts, swelling his force to tens of thousands, then advanced on Xingyuan until Military Governor Niu Cong fled the city. Yanhong declared himself acting governor, named Jian and others prefects of outlying districts, and kept them from taking their posts.

sentences.zh: 俄而晏宏正授節旄，恐部下謀己，多行忍虐，由是部眾離心。

translations.literal: Before long Yanhong received formal appointment with the insignia of command; fearing that his subordinates would plot against him, he often acted with cruelty, and thereby his troops lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yanhong received formal command with the ceremonial insignia. Fearing mutiny among his men, he ruled with growing cruelty, and his troops began to turn away from him.

sentences.zh: 建與別將韓建友善，晏宏益猜二建，偽待之厚，引入臥內。

translations.literal: Jian was on friendly terms with the deputy commander Han Jian; Yanhong grew all the more suspicious of the two Jians, feigned to treat them generously, and brought them into his private quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was close to the deputy commander Han Jian. Yanhong grew ever more suspicious of the two men named Jian, showered them with false kindness, and drew them into his sleeping quarters.

sentences.zh: 二建懼，夜登城慰守陴者，因月下共謀所向，謂韓建曰：「僕射甘言厚德，是疑我也，禍難無日矣，早宜擇利而行。

translations.literal: The two Jians were afraid; at night they climbed the wall to comfort the men on the battlements, and under the moonlight together discussed where to go; Wang Jian said to Han Jian, "The Vice Director's sweet words and generous treatment mean he suspects us; disaster is not far off—we should early choose what profits us and act."
translations.idiomatic: Both men were afraid. That night they climbed the wall to cheer the guards on the battlements and, in the moonlight, plotted their next move. Wang Jian told Han Jian, "The Vice Director's honeyed words and lavish favors mean he suspects us. Trouble will come any day now—we should seize our chance and leave while we can."

sentences.zh: 」韓曰：「善。

translations.literal: Han said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Han said, "Agreed."

sentences.zh: 」因率三千人趨行在，僖宗嘉之，賜與巨萬。

translations.literal: Thereupon they led three thousand men to hurry to the traveling court; Emperor Xizong commended them and bestowed tens of thousands in gifts.
translations.idiomatic: They then led three thousand men straight to the traveling court. Emperor Xizong praised them and rewarded them with a fortune.

sentences.zh: 分其兵為五都，仍以舊校主之，即晉暉、李師泰、張造與二建也，因號曰隨駕五都，田令孜皆錄為假子。

translations.literal: Their troops were divided into five commands, still led by their former commanders—namely Jin Hui, Li Shitai, Zhang Zao, and the two Jians—and were therefore called the Five Commands in Attendance on the Imperial Progress; Tian Lingzi enrolled them all as adoptive sons.
translations.idiomatic: Their force was split into five commands under their former commanders—Jin Hui, Li Shitai, Zhang Zao, and the two Jians—and became known as the Five Commands in Attendance on the Imperial Progress. Tian Lingzi took them all as adoptive sons.

sentences.zh: 及僖宗還宮，建等分典神策軍，皆遙領刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong returned to the palace, Jian and the others each took charge of part of the Shence Army, all holding prefectural posts in absentia.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong returned to the capital, Jian and the others each commanded a portion of the Shence Army while holding prefectural titles in name only.

sentences.zh: 光啟初，從僖宗再幸興元，令孜懼逼，求為西川監軍，楊復恭代為觀軍容使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Guangqi era, following Emperor Xizong on a second journey to Xingyuan, Lingzi, fearing pressure, requested appointment as supervising commissioner for Xichuan; Yang Fugong replaced him as Commissioner for Observing the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangqi reign, when the emperor again went to Xingyuan, Lingzi, fearing he was being cornered, asked to become supervising commissioner for Xichuan, and Yang Fugong took his place as Commissioner for Observing the Army.

sentences.zh: 建等素為令孜所厚，復恭懼不附己，乃出五將為郡守，以建為壁州刺史。

translations.literal: Jian and the others had long been favored by Lingzi; Fugong feared they would not attach themselves to him, and therefore sent the five generals out as prefectural administrators, appointing Jian prefect of Bi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and the others had long enjoyed Lingzi's favor. Fugong feared they would not side with him and posted the five generals as prefectural administrators, making Jian prefect of Bi.

sentences.zh: 天子還京，復恭以楊守亮鎮興元，尤畏建侵己，屢召之。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven returned to the capital, Fugong had Yang Shouliang garrison Xingyuan and especially feared that Jian would encroach on him, summoning him repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor returned to the capital, Fugong stationed Yang Shouliang at Xingyuan and, fearing Jian above all, summoned him again and again.

sentences.zh: 建不安其郡，因招合溪洞豪猾，有眾八千，寇閬州，陷之，復攻利州，刺史王珙棄城而去。

translations.literal: Jian was ill at ease in his prefecture; he therefore gathered fierce men from the stream valleys and cave districts, mustered eight thousand troops, raided Lang Prefecture and took it, then attacked Li Prefecture, where Prefect Wang Gong abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy in his post, Jian rallied tough men from the hill country and stream valleys until he had eight thousand followers. He stormed Lang Prefecture, took it, then attacked Li Prefecture, whose prefect Wang Gong fled the city.

sentences.zh: 建播剽二郡，所至殺掠，守亮不能制。

translations.literal: Jian spread plunder through the two prefectures; wherever he went he killed and looted, and Shouliang could not control him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian spread terror through both prefectures, killing and looting wherever he went, and Shouliang could not stop him.

sentences.zh: 東川節度使顧彥朗，初於關輔破賊時與建相聞，每遣人勞問，分貨幣軍食以給之，故建不侵梓、遂。

translations.literal: Gu Yanlang, military governor of Dongchuan, had first become acquainted with Jian when breaking the rebels in the Guanzhong region; he often sent men to inquire after him and shared goods, money, and army provisions to supply him, and therefore Jian did not invade Zi and Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yanlang, military governor of Dongchuan, had known Jian since the campaigns against the rebels in the Guanzhong region. He sent envoys with gifts and shared money and army rations with him, so Jian left Zi and Sui Prefectures alone.

sentences.zh: 西川節度使陳敬瑄憂其膠固，謀於監軍田令孜，曰：「王八，吾子也，彼無他腸，作賊山南，實進退無歸故也。

translations.literal: Chen Jingxuan, military governor of Xichuan, worried that Jian was entrenched and took counsel with the supervising commissioner Tian Lingzi, saying, "Wang the Eighth is my son; he has no other designs—his banditry in Shannan is really because he has nowhere to advance or retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan, military governor of Xichuan, worried that Jian had dug in too deep and consulted the supervising commissioner Tian Lingzi. "Wang the Eighth is my adopted son," he said. "He has no hidden agenda. He turned bandit in Shannan only because he had nowhere else to go."

sentences.zh: 吾馳咫尺之書，可以坐置麾下。

translations.literal: If I send a letter a foot long, I can seat him under my command without moving."
translations.idiomatic: A single letter from me will bring him under my banner without my stirring from my seat."

sentences.zh: 」即飛書招建。

translations.literal: He immediately sent a swift letter summoning Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He at once sent an urgent summons to Jian.

sentences.zh: 建大喜，遣使謂彥朗曰：「監軍阿父遣信見招，仆欲諸成都省阿父，因依陳太師得一大郡，是所願也。

translations.literal: Jian was greatly pleased and sent an envoy to tell Yanlang, "The supervising commissioner, my adoptive father, has sent a message summoning me; your servant wishes to go to Chengdu to visit my adoptive father and, relying on Grand Preceptor Chen, obtain a large prefecture—that is what I desire."
translations.idiomatic: Jian was delighted and sent word to Yanlang: "My adoptive father the supervising commissioner has summoned me. I mean to go to Chengdu to see him and, with Grand Preceptor Chen's backing, win a major prefecture—that is all I want."

sentences.zh: 」即之梓州見彥朗，留家寄東川，選精甲三千之成都。

translations.literal: He thereupon went to Zizhou to see Yanlang, left his family in Dongchuan as a deposit, and selected three thousand picked armored troops to go to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Zizhou to see Yanlang, left his family in Dongchuan as hostages, and marched three thousand picked armored troops toward Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 行次鹿頭，或謂敬瑄曰：「建，今之劇賊，鴟視狼顧，專謀人國邑，儻其即至，公以何等處之？

translations.literal: When he reached Lutou, someone said to Jingxuan, "Jian is today's fierce bandit—he looks like an owl and glances like a wolf, bent solely on seizing others' states and cities; if he should arrive at once, with what rank will you receive him?"
translations.idiomatic: At Lutou Pass someone warned Jingxuan, "Jian is the fiercest bandit alive—rapacious, restless, bent on seizing every domain he can reach. If he arrives tomorrow, how do you mean to treat him?"

sentences.zh: 彼建雄心，終不居人之下，公如以將校遇之，是養虎自貽其患也。

translations.literal: That Jian has a great heart and will never remain beneath others; if you treat him as a mere commander, you are rearing a tiger and bringing trouble on yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Jian has grand ambitions and will never serve under another man. If you receive him as an ordinary commander, you will be raising a tiger to devour you later."

sentences.zh: 」敬瑄懼，乃遣人止建，遽修城守。

translations.literal: Jingxuan was afraid and therefore sent men to stop Jian, hastily repairing the walls and preparing the defense.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan took fright, sent men to turn Jian back, and hurriedly strengthened the city's defenses.

sentences.zh: 建怒，遂據漢州，領輕兵至成都。

translations.literal: Jian was enraged, thereupon seized Han Prefecture, and led light troops to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Jian seized Han Prefecture and led light troops straight to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄讓之曰：「若何為者，而犯吾疆理？

translations.literal: Jingxuan reproached him, saying, "What are you doing, encroaching on my territory?"
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan rebuked him: "What do you think you are doing, violating my borders?"

sentences.zh: 」建軍吏報曰：「閬州司徒比寄東川，而軍容太師使者繼召，今復拒絕，何也？

translations.literal: Jian's staff officer replied, "The Minister of Works of Lang Prefecture recently left his family in Dongchuan as a deposit, while envoys of the Commissioner for Observing the Army and the Grand Preceptor summoned him one after another; now you refuse him again—why?"
translations.idiomatic: An officer from Jian's staff answered, "The Minister of Works of Lang recently left his family in Dongchuan as hostages while the Commissioner for Observing the Army and the Grand Preceptor's envoys summoned him again and again. Why do you turn him away now?"

sentences.zh: 司徒不惜改轅而東，來北省太師，反為拒絕，慮顧梓州復相嫌間，謂我何心故也。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works did not spare himself in changing course eastward to come north and visit the Grand Preceptor, yet was refused in return; he fears that Gu of Zizhou will again be set at odds with him and wonder what his intentions are.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Works changed course and marched east to pay his respects to the Grand Preceptor, only to be turned away. He fears Gu of Zizhou will take this as proof of bad faith and wonder what he is really after.

sentences.zh: 使我來報，且欲寄食漢州，公勿復疑。

translations.literal: He sent me to report and also wishes to quarter his troops on provisions from Han Prefecture—do not doubt him further."
translations.idiomatic: He sent me to explain that he only wants to quarter his men on Han Prefecture's supplies—please put your suspicions to rest."

sentences.zh: 」時光啟三年。

translations.literal: It was the third year of Guangqi.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the third year of Guangqi.

sentences.zh: 居浹旬，建盡取東川之眾，設梯沖攻成都，三日不克而退，復保漢州。

translations.literal: After about ten days, Jian gathered all the forces of Dongchuan, set up scaling ladders and battering rams, and attacked Chengdu; after three days he could not take it and withdrew, again holding Han Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days Jian mustered every soldier he could draw from Dongchuan, raised scaling ladders and battering rams, and assaulted Chengdu. After three days of failure he withdrew and fell back on Han Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 月餘，大剽蜀土，進逼彭州，百道攻之，敬瑄出兵來援，建解圍，縱兵大掠，十一州皆罹其毒，民不聊生。

translations.literal: After more than a month he carried out great plunder throughout Shu territory, advanced and pressed Peng Prefecture, attacking it from a hundred directions; Jingxuan sent troops to relieve it; Jian lifted the siege and let his soldiers plunder on a grand scale; eleven prefectures all suffered his harm, and the people could not sustain life.
translations.idiomatic: For more than a month he ravaged Shu, then closed on Peng Prefecture and attacked from every side. When Jingxuan sent relief, Jian broke off the siege and unleashed his men in a wider rampage. Eleven prefectures felt his scourge, and the people could barely survive.

sentences.zh: 建軍勢日盛，復攻成都，敬瑄患之，顧彥朗亦懼侵己。

translations.literal: Jian's military strength grew daily; he again attacked Chengdu; Jingxuan was troubled by it, and Gu Yanlang also feared he would encroach on himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's army grew stronger by the day, and he attacked Chengdu again. Jingxuan was alarmed, and Gu Yanlang feared he would be next.

sentences.zh: 昭宗即位，彥朗表請雪建，擇大臣為蜀帥，移敬瑄他鎮，乃詔宰臣韋昭度鎮蜀，以代敬瑄。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong took the throne, Yanlang memorialized requesting that Jian be cleared of guilt, that a senior minister be chosen as commander of Shu, and that Jingxuan be transferred to another post; thereupon an edict appointed the chief minister Wei Zhaodu to garrison Shu in place of Jingxuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhaozong came to the throne, Yanlang memorialized asking that Jian be pardoned, that a senior minister be sent to command Shu, and that Jingxuan be moved elsewhere. The court then ordered Chief Minister Wei Zhaodu to take command of Shu in Jingxuan's place.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄不受代，天子怒，命顧彥朗、楊守亮討之，時昭度以建為牙內都校，董其部兵。

translations.literal: Jingxuan would not accept replacement; the Son of Heaven was angry and ordered Gu Yanlang and Yang Shouliang to campaign against him; at that time Zhaodu made Jian commander within the headquarters guard and supervised his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan refused to step down. The emperor was furious and ordered Gu Yanlang and Yang Shouliang to attack him. Zhaodu meanwhile made Jian commander of the headquarters guard and put him in charge of his own troops.

sentences.zh: （《鑒戒錄》云：昭度以部兵置行府。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Jianjie Lu》 says: Zhaodu stationed his own troops and established a field headquarters.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (According to the 《Jianjie Lu》, Zhaodu stationed his own troops and set up a field headquarters.)]

sentences.zh: 及王師無功，建謂昭度曰：「相公興數萬之眾，討賊未效，餉運交不相屬。

translations.literal: When the imperial army achieved no success, Jian said to Zhaodu, "Your Excellency has raised tens of thousands of men, yet the campaign against the rebel has not succeeded, and supply transports one after another fail to connect.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial campaign failed, Jian told Zhaodu, "Your Excellency raised an army of tens of thousands, yet the expedition against the rebel has accomplished nothing, and supply trains no longer keep pace.

sentences.zh: 近聞遷洛以來，藩鎮相噬，朝廷姑息不暇，與其勞師以事蠻方，不如從而赦之，且以兵威靖中原，是國之本也。

translations.literal: I have lately heard that since the move to Luoyang, the military governors have devoured one another and the court has had no leisure for indulgence; rather than wear out the army on the barbarian south, it would be better to follow this course and pardon him, and moreover use military might to pacify the central plains—that is the foundation of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Since the court moved back to Luoyang, the provinces have been tearing one another apart and the throne has barely kept up. Rather than exhaust the army in the southern wilds, you would do better to pardon the rebel and turn your soldiers' strength to pacifying the central plains—that is the root of the realm.

sentences.zh: 相公盍歸朝覲，與主上畫之。

translations.literal: Why does Your Excellency not return to court for an audience and discuss the matter with the sovereign?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Excellency should return to court, present yourself to the throne, and lay out the plan there."

sentences.zh: 」昭度持疑未決。

translations.literal: Zhaodu remained in doubt and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaodu hesitated and could not make up his mind.

sentences.zh: 一日，建陰令軍士於行府門外擒昭度親吏，臠而食之，建徐啟昭度曰：「蓋軍士乏食，以至於是耶！

translations.literal: One day Jian secretly ordered soldiers outside the field headquarters gate to seize one of Zhaodu's close clerks, cut him to pieces, and eat him; Jian then slowly opened the matter to Zhaodu, saying, "Perhaps the soldiers lacked food and came to this?"
translations.idiomatic: One day Jian secretly had his soldiers seize one of Zhaodu's personal clerks outside the field headquarters, butcher him, and eat his flesh. Jian then told Zhaodu calmly, "I suppose the men were simply out of food and driven to this?"

sentences.zh: 」昭度大懼，遂留符節與建，即日東還。

translations.literal: Zhaodu was greatly afraid, left the tally and insignia with Jian, and that same day returned east.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Zhaodu left his credentials with Jian and headed east the same day.

sentences.zh: 才出劍門，建即嚴兵守門，不納東師。

translations.literal: As soon as he had passed Jianmen, Jian at once stationed troops in strength to guard the gate and would not admit the eastern army.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had he passed through Jianmen Pass when Jian sealed the gate with a strong guard and refused to let the eastern army follow.

sentences.zh: 月餘，建攻西川管內八州，所至響應，遂急攻成都，田令孜登城謂建曰：「老夫與八哥相厚，太師久以知聞，有何嫌恨，如是困我之甚耶！

translations.literal: After more than a month Jian attacked the eight prefectures within the Xichuan circuit; wherever he went there was response; he then pressed the attack on Chengdu; Tian Lingzi mounted the wall and said to Jian, "This old man and Brother the Eighth have long been close; the Grand Preceptor has known this for a long time—what resentment is there, that you should distress me so severely?"
translations.idiomatic: Within a month Jian overran eight prefectures in the Xichuan circuit, meeting welcome everywhere he marched, then pressed hard on Chengdu. Tian Lingzi climbed the wall and called down to Jian, "Your old adoptive father and Brother the Eighth have always been close, and the Grand Preceptor has known it for years. What grudge could justify pressing us this hard?"

sentences.zh: 」建曰：「軍容父子之恩，心何敢忘，但天子付以兵柄，太師孤絕朝廷故也。

translations.literal: Jian said, "The father-and-son kindness between the Commissioner for Observing the Army and myself—how could my heart dare forget it? But the Son of Heaven entrusted you with military authority because the Grand Preceptor has cut himself off from the court."
translations.idiomatic: Jian answered, "How could I forget the bond between adoptive father and son? But the emperor gave you the army because the Grand Preceptor has cut himself off from the court."

sentences.zh: 茍太師悉心改圖，何福如之！

translations.literal: If the Grand Preceptor will wholeheartedly change his course, what blessing could compare!"
translations.idiomatic: If the Grand Preceptor will truly change course, what greater fortune could there be!"

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「吾欲與八哥軍中相款，如何？

translations.literal: He also said, "I wish to meet Brother the Eighth in the camp for a cordial visit—how would that be?"
translations.idiomatic: He added, "I would like to meet Brother the Eighth in camp for a friendly visit. Would that suit you?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「父子之義，何嫌也。

translations.literal: He said, "In the bond between father and son, what suspicion is there?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Between father and son, what cause for suspicion could there be?"

sentences.zh: 」是夜，令孜攜蜀帥符印入建軍授建。

translations.literal: That night Lingzi carried the tally and seal of the Shu commander into Jian's army and handed them to Jian.
translations.idiomatic: That night Lingzi entered Jian's camp carrying the commander of Shu's tally and seal and surrendered them to him.

sentences.zh: 建泣謝曰：「太師初心太過，致有今日相戾，既此推心，一切如舊。

translations.literal: Jian wept and thanked him, saying, "The Grand Preceptor's original intent went too far and brought about today's estrangement; now that you have opened your heart to me, all is as before."
translations.idiomatic: Jian wept and thanked him. "The Grand Preceptor's first intentions went too far and brought us to this breach," he said. "Now that you have opened your heart to me, let everything be as it was."

sentences.zh: 」翌日，敬瑄啟關迎建，以蜀帥讓之，建乃自稱留後，表陳其事。

translations.literal: The next day Jingxuan opened the gates to welcome Jian and yielded the Shu command to him; Jian thereupon styled himself acting governor and memorialized stating the facts.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Jingxuan opened the gates to welcome Jian and yielded command of Shu to him. Jian declared himself acting governor and memorialized the court on what had happened.

sentences.zh: 明年春，制授檢校太傅、成都尹、西川節度副大使知節度事、管內觀察處置、雲南八國招撫等使，時龍紀元年也。

translations.literal: In the spring of the following year an edict appointed him Acting Grand Preceptor, Prefect of Chengdu, deputy military governor of Xichuan with authority over military affairs, commissioner for observation and disposition within the circuit, and commissioner for pacifying the eight kingdoms of Yunnan, among other posts; it was the first year of Longji.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring an edict made him Acting Grand Preceptor, Prefect of Chengdu, deputy military governor of Xichuan with full authority over the circuit, and commissioner for observation, disposition, and pacification of the eight kingdoms of Yunnan. This was in the first year of Longji.

sentences.zh: 移敬瑄於雅州安置，仍以其子為刺史，既行，建令人殺之於路，令孜仍舊監軍事。

translations.literal: Jingxuan was transferred to be settled at Ya Prefecture, and his son was still made prefect; after they had set out, Jian sent men to kill them on the road; Lingzi continued as before in supervising military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan was transferred to Ya Prefecture for detention, with his son left as prefect there. Once they had set out, Jian had them killed on the road. Lingzi continued to supervise military affairs as before.

sentences.zh: 數月，或告令孜通鳳翔書問，下獄餓死。

translations.literal: Several months later someone reported that Lingzi was in correspondence with Fengxiang; he was imprisoned and starved to death.
translations.idiomatic: Months later someone accused Lingzi of secret correspondence with Fengxiang. He was thrown into prison and starved to death.

sentences.zh: （《蜀梼杌》云：「敬瑄廢處雅州，以其子為刺史。

translations.literal: (The 《Shu Taowu》 says: "Jingxuan was deposed and settled at Ya Prefecture, with his son made prefect.
translations.idiomatic: (According to the 《Shu Taowu》, "Jingxuan was deposed and confined at Ya Prefecture, with his son left as prefect.

sentences.zh: 既行，建遣殺於三江，令孜仍監其軍，復以令孜陰附鳳翔，下獄餓死。）〉

translations.literal: After they set out, Jian sent men to kill them at Sanjiang; Lingzi still supervised his army; again because Lingzi secretly attached himself to Fengxiang, he was imprisoned and starved to death.")〉
translations.idiomatic: After they set out, Jian had them killed at Sanjiang. Lingzi continued to supervise the army until he was again accused of secretly siding with Fengxiang, imprisoned, and starved to death.")]

sentences.zh: 建雄猜多機略，意常難測，既有蜀土，復欲窺伺東川，又以彥朗婚姻之舊，未果行。

translations.literal: Jian was fierce, suspicious, and full of stratagems; his intentions were often hard to fathom; once he possessed Shu territory he again wished to spy out an opportunity against Dongchuan, but because of his old ties of marriage with Yanlang he did not yet act.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was fierce, suspicious, and endlessly scheming, his intentions hard to read. Once he held Shu he again cast his eye on Dongchuan, but the marriage tie with Yanlang still held him back for a time.

sentences.zh: 會彥朗卒，弟彥暉代為梓帥，交情稍怠。

translations.literal: When Yanlang died, his younger brother Yanhui replaced him as commander of Zi, and their friendship gradually cooled.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanlang died, his younger brother Yanhui took command at Zi, and the old friendship began to fray.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞乘其有間，密構彥暉，因與茂貞連盟，關征疆吏之間，與蜀人得失。

translations.literal: Li Maozhen seized the opening between them and secretly won over Yanhui; he therefore allied with Maozhen; at the passes and frontier posts the border officials contended over gains and losses with the people of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen seized the breach between them and secretly won Yanhui over, drawing him into an alliance. At the frontier passes the border officials and the men of Shu traded blows over every advantage gained or lost.

sentences.zh: 大順末，建出師攻梓州，彥暉求援於鳳翔，李茂貞出師援之，建即圍解，自是秦、川交惡者累年。

translations.literal: At the end of Dashun, Jian marched out to attack Zizhou; Yanhui sought aid from Fengxiang; Li Maozhen marched out to relieve him; Jian thereupon lifted the siege; from this time Qin and Chuan were at odds for many years.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Dashun era Jian marched on Zizhou. Yanhui called on Fengxiang for help, and Li Maozhen marched to his relief, forcing Jian to raise the siege. From then on Qin and Shu were enemies for years.

sentences.zh: 後建大起蜀軍，敗岐、梓之兵於利州，彥暉懼，乞和，請與岐人絕，許之。

translations.literal: Later Jian raised the Shu army on a great scale and defeated the Qi and Zi forces at Li Prefecture; Yanhui was afraid, begged for peace, and asked to break with the Qi people; Jian agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jian mobilized a great Shu army and routed the Qi and Zi forces at Li Prefecture. Terrified, Yanhui sued for peace and asked to cut ties with the Qi domain. Jian agreed.

sentences.zh: 景福中，山南之師寇東川，彥暉求援於建，建出兵赴之，大敗興元之眾。

translations.literal: In the Jingfu era, the Shannan army raided Dongchuan; Yanhui sought aid from Jian; Jian sent troops to his relief and inflicted a great defeat on the Xingyuan forces.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingfu reign the Shannan army invaded Dongchuan. Yanhui appealed to Jian, who marched to his aid and crushed the Xingyuan troops.

sentences.zh: 洎軍旋，建承虛奄襲梓州，據彥暉，置於成都，遂兼有兩川，自此軍鋒益熾。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Jian took advantage of the moment to make a sudden attack on Zizhou, seized Yanhui, and placed him in Chengdu; he thereby held both Chuan circuits, and from this time his military edge grew all the fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return Jian struck Zizhou while it was exposed, seized Yanhui, and kept him in Chengdu. He now held both Chuan circuits, and his armies grew fiercer than ever.

sentences.zh: 天復初，李茂貞、韓全誨劫遷車駕在鳳翔，梁祖攻圍歷年。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu, Li Maozhen and Han Quanhui seized and moved the imperial carriage to Fengxiang; the Liang founder besieged them for years.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianfu era Li Maozhen and Han Quanhui seized the emperor and held him at Fengxiang while the Liang founder besieged them year after year.

sentences.zh: 建外修好於汴，指茂貞罪狀，又陰與茂貞間使往來，且言堅壁勿和，許以出師赴援，因分命諸軍攻取興元。

translations.literal: Outwardly Jian cultivated good relations with Bian, denouncing Maozhen's crimes; secretly he also exchanged envoys with Maozhen, telling him to hold his walls and not make peace, promising to march out in relief, and meanwhile ordering his various armies to attack and take Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly Jian courted Bian and denounced Maozhen's crimes. In secret he exchanged envoys with Maozhen, urging him to hold his walls and refuse peace while promising relief, and at the same time ordered his armies to seize Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 比及梁祖解圍，茂貞山南諸州皆為建所有，自置守將。

translations.literal: By the time the Liang founder lifted the siege, all Maozhen's prefectures in Shannan were in Jian's possession, and he himself appointed defending generals.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the Liang founder lifted the siege, Jian held all of Maozhen's Shannan prefectures and appointed his own garrison commanders.

sentences.zh: 及茂貞垂翅，天子遷雒陽，建復攻茂貞之秦、隴等州，茂貞削弱不能守。

translations.literal: When Maozhen's wings were clipped and the Son of Heaven moved to Luoyang, Jian again attacked Maozhen's Qin, Long, and other prefectures; Maozhen was weakened and could not hold them.
translations.idiomatic: When Maozhen's power collapsed and the emperor moved to Luoyang, Jian attacked Maozhen's Qin, Long, and other prefectures again. Maozhen was too weak to hold them.

sentences.zh: 或勸建因取鳳翔，建曰：「此言失策，吾所得已多，不俟復增岐下。

translations.literal: Someone urged Jian to take advantage of the moment and seize Fengxiang; Jian said, "This advice is a mistaken stratagem. What I have already gained is ample; there is no need to add more under the Qi domain.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Jian to seize Fengxiang while he could. Jian said, "That would be a mistake. I already hold more than enough; there is no need to add the Qi capital as well.

sentences.zh: 茂貞雖常才，然名望宿素，與朱公力爭不足，守境有餘。

translations.literal: Maozhen, though only of ordinary talent, has long-standing fame and standing; he is not strong enough to contend with Lord Zhu, yet more than adequate to guard his borders.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen is only a man of ordinary ability, but his name and standing are old and weighty. He cannot match Lord Zhu in a contest of force, yet he can hold his borders well enough.

sentences.zh: 韓生所謂入為扞蔽，出為席藉是也。

translations.literal: This is what Master Han meant by serving within as a shield and barrier and serving without as mat and cushion."
translations.idiomatic: This is what Han Fei meant when he said a state needs shields within and mats without."

sentences.zh: 適宜援而固之，為吾盾鹵耳。

translations.literal: It is fitting to support and strengthen him and make him my shield and rampart."
translations.idiomatic: The right move is to support him and keep him strong as my shield on the frontier."

sentences.zh: 」及梁祖將謀強禪，建與諸藩同謀興復，乃令其將康晏率兵三萬會於鳳翔，數與汴將王重師戰，不利而還。

translations.literal: When the Liang founder was about to plot forced abdication, Jian joined the other military governors in a plan to restore the dynasty; he therefore ordered his general Kang Yan to lead thirty thousand men to assemble at Fengxiang; they fought several times with the Bian general Wang Chongshi and, meeting no success, returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang founder prepared to force the throne from the Tang, Jian joined the other governors in a plan to restore the dynasty and sent his general Kang Yan with thirty thousand men to Fengxiang. Kang Yan clashed repeatedly with the Bian general Wang Chongshi, failed, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 趙匡凝之失荊、襄也，弟匡明以其幹奔蜀，建因得夔、峽、忠、萬等州。

translations.literal: When Zhao Kuangning lost Jing and Xiang, his younger brother Kuangming fled to Shu with his staff; Jian thereby obtained the prefectures of Kui, Xia, Zhong, Wan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Kuangning lost Jing and Xiang, his brother Kuangming fled to Shu with his staff. Jian thereby gained Kui, Xia, Zhong, Wan, and the other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 及梁祖開國，蜀人請建行劉備故事。

translations.literal: When the Liang founder founded his state, the people of Shu asked Jian to follow Liu Bei's precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang founder founded his dynasty, the people of Shu urged Jian to follow Liu Bei's example and declare himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 建自帝於成都，改元永平。

translations.literal: Jian declared himself emperor at Chengdu and changed the era name to Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: Jian declared himself emperor at Chengdu and proclaimed the Yongping era.

sentences.zh: 五年，改元通正。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he changed the era name to Tongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: In his fifth year he changed the era name to Tongzheng.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，改元天漢，又改元光天。

translations.literal: That winter he changed the era name to Tianhan, and again to Guangtian.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he changed the era to Tianhan, then again to Guangtian.

sentences.zh: 在位十二年，年七十二。

translations.literal: He reigned twelve years and died at seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He reigned twelve years and died at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 子衍嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yan succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 衍，建之幼子也。

translations.literal: Yan was Jian's youngest son.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was Jian's youngest son.

sentences.zh: 建卒，衍襲偽位，改元乾德。

translations.literal: When Jian died, Yan succeeded to the usurper's throne and changed the era name to Qiande.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian died, Yan took the throne and proclaimed the Qiande era.

sentences.zh: 六年十二月，改明年為鹹康。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the sixth year he changed the following year to Xian'kang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of his sixth year he renamed the coming year Xian'kang.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，衍奉其母、徐妃同遊於青城山，駐於上清宮。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn Yan escorted his mother and Consort Xu on a tour to Mount Qingcheng and lodged at the Shangqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Yan took his mother and Consort Xu on an excursion to Mount Qingcheng and stayed at the Shangqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 時宮人皆衣道服，頂金蓮花冠，衣畫雲霞，望之若神仙，及侍宴，酒酣，皆免冠而退，則其髻髽然。

translations.literal: At that time the palace women all wore Daoist robes, topped with golden lotus crowns, their garments painted with clouds and mist; viewed from afar they seemed like immortals; when they attended the banquet and the wine was deep, they all removed their caps and withdrew, and then their topknots stood up plainly.
translations.idiomatic: The palace women all wore Daoist robes and golden lotus crowns, their garments painted with clouds and mist so that from a distance they looked like immortals. When they served at the banquet and the wine had gone deep, they removed their caps and withdrew, revealing their topknots plainly.

sentences.zh: 又構怡神亭，以佞臣韓昭等為狎客，雜以婦人，以恣荒宴，或自旦至暮，繼之以燭。

translations.literal: He also built the Yishen Pavilion, taking the flatterers Han Zhao and others as intimate guests, mixing in women, and indulging in dissolute feasting; sometimes from dawn to dusk, continuing with candles.
translations.idiomatic: He also built the Yishen Pavilion, where flatterers such as Han Zhao served as his boon companions amid a crowd of women, and he gave himself over to reckless revelry that sometimes ran from dawn to dusk by candlelight.

sentences.zh: 偽嘉王宗壽侍宴，因以社稷國政為言，言發涕流，至於再三。

translations.literal: The usurper Prince of Jia, Zongshou, attended the banquet and spoke of the altars of state and national affairs; as he spoke tears flowed, and this happened again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zongshou of Jia attended the banquet and spoke of the realm and its government, weeping as he did so, again and again.

sentences.zh: 同宴佞臣潘在迎等並奏衍云：「嘉王好酒悲。

translations.literal: The flatterers at the same banquet, Pan Zaiying and others, all reported to Yan, saying, "Prince Jia loves wine and weeps."
translations.idiomatic: The flatterers at the same table, Pan Zaiying and the rest, all told Yan, "Prince Jia is a drunk who weeps over his cups."

sentences.zh: 」因翻恣諧謔，取笑而罷。

translations.literal: Thereupon they turned to unrestrained jest and banter, made sport of him, and the matter ended.
translations.idiomatic: They then turned the evening to coarse jokes and ridicule until the matter was laughed away.

sentences.zh: 自是忠正之臣結舌矣。

translations.literal: From this time loyal and upright ministers held their tongues.
translations.idiomatic: From that day forward loyal ministers held their tongues.

sentences.zh: 時中國多故，衍得以自安。

translations.literal: At that time the central realm was beset by many troubles, and Yan was thereby able to remain secure.
translations.idiomatic: With the central realm torn by turmoil, Yan was left undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗平梁，遣使告捷於蜀，蜀人恟懼，致禮復命，稱「大蜀國主致書上大唐皇帝」，詞理稍抗，莊宗不能容，遣客省使李嚴報聘，且市宮中珍玩，蜀人皆禁而不出。

translations.literal: Tang Emperor Zhuangzong pacified Liang and sent envoys to announce victory to Shu; the people of Shu were alarmed and fearful, sent gifts in reply, and addressed their message as "The Lord of Great Shu writes to present to the Emperor of Great Tang"; the wording was somewhat defiant; Zhuangzong could not tolerate it and sent the guest-bureau envoy Li Yan on a return visit, also wishing to purchase rare treasures from the palace; the people of Shu all forbade them and would not let them out.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang Emperor Zhuangzong conquered Liang, he sent envoys to announce victory in Shu. The Shu court was alarmed and sent a formal reply addressed as "The Lord of Great Shu writes to the Emperor of Great Tang," with wording just defiant enough to offend Zhuangzong. He sent the guest-bureau envoy Li Yan on a return mission and sought to buy palace treasures, but the Shu authorities refused to let any of them leave.

sentences.zh: 衍既沖呆，軍國之政，鹹委於人。

translations.literal: Since Yan was simple-minded and dull, military and state affairs were all entrusted to others.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was childish and dull, and he left military and civil affairs entirely to others.

sentences.zh: 有王宗弼者，為六軍使，總外任；

translations.literal: There was one Wang Zongbi, who served as commander of the Six Armies and oversaw external assignments;
translations.idiomatic: One Wang Zongbi served as commander of the Six Armies and held overall authority in the field;

sentences.zh: 宋光嗣者，為樞密使，總內任。

translations.literal: Song Guangsi served as commissioner of confidential affairs and oversaw internal assignments.
translations.idiomatic: Song Guangsi served as commissioner of confidential affairs and controlled affairs within the court.

sentences.zh: 洎嚴至蜀，光嗣等曲宴，因言中國近事，嚴亦引近事折之，語在嚴傳。

translations.literal: When Yan arrived in Shu, Guangsi and others gave him a private banquet and spoke of recent events in the central realm; Yan also cited recent events to refute them; the account is in Yan's biography.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan reached Shu, Guangsi and others entertained him privately and spoke of recent events in the central realm. Yan answered with recent events of his own to refute them; the full exchange appears in his biography.

sentences.zh: 光嗣等聞嚴辯對，畏而奇之。

translations.literal: Guangsi and the others heard Yan's rebuttals, feared him, and regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Guangsi and his colleagues heard Yan's sharp replies, feared him, and marveled at his ability.

sentences.zh: 及嚴使還，奏莊宗曰：「王衍呆童耳，宗弼等總其兵柄，但益家財，不恤民事，君臣上下，惟務窮奢。

translations.literal: When Yan returned from his mission he reported to Zhuangzong, saying, "Wang Yan is a foolish child; Zongbi and the others hold military authority but only increase their household wealth and do not care for the people's affairs; ruler and ministers above and below devote themselves solely to extreme luxury.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Yan reported to Zhuangzong, "Wang Yan is a witless boy. Zongbi and the rest hold the army but care only to enrich their households, not the people's welfare. Court and camp alike pursue nothing but extravagance.

sentences.zh: 其舊勛故老，棄而不任，蠻蜓蜑之人，痛深瘡痏。

translations.literal: Their old meritorious ministers and elders are cast aside and not employed; the southern tribal peoples suffer wounds deep as running sores.
translations.idiomatic: Old ministers of merit are cast aside, while the tribal peoples of the south bear grievances like open sores.

sentences.zh: 以臣料之，大兵一臨，望風瓦解。

translations.literal: By my estimate, when a great army arrives they will collapse at the first wind.
translations.idiomatic: In my judgment, when a great army arrives they will crumble at the first sight of it.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗深然之，遂蒐兵括馬，有平蜀之志。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong deeply agreed and thereupon gathered troops and rounded up horses, cherishing the aim of pacifying Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong agreed wholeheartedly, gathered troops and horses, and set his mind on conquering Shu.

sentences.zh: 唐師未起時，偽東川節度使宋承葆獻計於衍云：「唐國兵強，不早為謀，後將焉救？

translations.literal: Before the Tang army marched, the usurper military governor of Dongchuan Song Chengbao offered a plan to Yan, saying, "The Tang state is militarily strong; if we do not plan early, how shall we be saved later?
translations.idiomatic: Before the Tang campaign began, the Dongchuan military governor Song Chengbao urged Yan, "Tang armies are strong. If we do not act now, how will we save ourselves later?

sentences.zh: 請於嘉州沿江造戰艦五百艘，募水軍五千，自江下峽，臣以東師出襄、鄧，水陸俱進，東北沿邊，嚴兵據險。

translations.literal: I ask that five hundred warships be built along the river at Jia Prefecture and five thousand naval troops recruited; descending the river through the gorges, while I lead eastern forces out from Xiang and Deng, advancing by land and water together, along the northeastern frontier stationing troops in strength to hold the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Build five hundred warships at Jia Prefecture along the river and raise five thousand sailors to descend through the gorges, while I lead eastern forces from Xiang and Deng so that land and water advance together. Along the northeastern frontier, hold the passes with strong garrisons.

sentences.zh: 南師出江陵，利則進取，否則退保硤口。

translations.literal: Southern forces should march from Jiangling; if advantageous, advance and seize ground, otherwise fall back and hold Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Send southern forces from Jiangling to advance when the moment favors them, or fall back and hold Xiakou if it does not.

sentences.zh: 又選三蜀驍壯三萬，急攻岐、雍，東據河、潼，北招契丹，啖以美利，見可則進，否則據散關以固吾圉，事縱不捷，亦攻敵人之心矣。

translations.literal: Further select thirty thousand fierce warriors of the Three Shu, strike Qi and Yong in haste, hold the east at He and Tong, summon the Khitan in the north and entice them with rich profit; advance when there is opportunity, otherwise hold Sanguan Pass to secure our borders; even if the plan does not succeed, it will still strike at the enemy's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Choose thirty thousand of Shu's best fighters, strike Qi and Yong swiftly, seize He and Tong in the east, and summon the Khitan in the north with rich rewards. Advance when the chance is ripe; otherwise hold Sanguan Pass to secure our borders. Even if the plan fails, it will shake the enemy's resolve.

sentences.zh: 」衍不從。

translations.literal: Yan did not follow it.
translations.idiomatic: Yan refused.

sentences.zh: 唐同光三年九月十日，莊宗下制伐蜀，命興聖宮使魏王繼岌為都統，樞密使郭崇韜為行營都招討。

translations.literal: On the tenth day of the ninth month of the third year of Tongguang of Tang, Zhuangzong issued an edict to campaign against Shu, appointing the Prince of Wei Jiji, envoy of the Xingsheng Palace, as overall commander and the commissioner of confidential affairs Guo Chongtao as overall commander of the field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On the tenth day of the ninth month of Tongguang year 3, Zhuangzong ordered a campaign against Shu, naming Prince of Wei Jiji overall commander and Commissioner Guo Chongtao commander of the field army.

sentences.zh: 其月十八日，魏王統闕下諸軍發洛陽。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth day of that month the Prince of Wei led the armies of the court out from Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth of that month the Prince of Wei led the imperial armies out of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 十一月二十一日，魏王至德陽，衍報云：「比與將校謀歸國，偽樞密使宋光嗣、景潤澄，南北院宣徽使李周輅、歐陽晃等四人異謀熒惑，臣各已處斬，今送納首級。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day of the eleventh month the Prince of Wei reached Deyang; Yan reported, saying, "Recently I plotted with the generals to return to allegiance, but the usurper commissioners of confidential affairs Song Guangsi and Jing Runcheng and the commissioners of the northern and southern bureaus Li Zhou'e and Ouyang Huang, four men in all, pursued a different plot and misled the court; I have already executed each of them and now send their heads.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first of the eleventh month the Prince of Wei reached Deyang. Yan reported that he had lately plotted with his generals to submit to Tang, but Song Guangsi, Jing Runcheng, Li Zhou'e, and Ouyang Huang had led him astray with a rival plot. He had executed all four and now sent their heads.

sentences.zh: 」是日，衍上表曰：「臣衍先人建，久在坤維，受先朝寵澤，一開土宇，將四十年。

translations.literal: That same day Yan submitted a memorial, saying, "Your subject Yan's forebear Jian long dwelt in the southwest, received the former dynasty's favor, opened a domain, and has ruled for nearly forty years.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Yan memorialized the throne: "Your subject's forebear Jian long held the southwest, received the former dynasty's grace, opened a realm, and has ruled for nearly forty years.

sentences.zh: 頃以梁孽興災，洪圖版蕩，不可助逆，遂乃從權，勉徇眾情，止王三旬，固非獲已，未有所歸。

translations.literal: Recently because the Liang calamity arose and the great design was overturned, I could not aid rebellion and therefore followed expediency, striving to satisfy popular feeling, reigning as king for only thirty days—it was truly not my wish, and I had nowhere to turn.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang rebellion convulsed the realm I could not aid treason and bowed to necessity, ruling as king for only thirty days to satisfy my people. It was never my choice, and I had nowhere else to turn.

sentences.zh: 臣輒紹鎡基，且安生聚。

translations.literal: Your subject thereupon continued the foundation and sought to settle the people.
translations.idiomatic: I then carried on the foundation he laid and sought only to settle my people.

sentences.zh: 臣衍誠惶誠恐，伏惟皇帝陛下，嗣堯、舜之業，陳湯、武之師，廓定寰區，削平兇逆，梯航垂集，文軌混同。

translations.literal: Your subject Yan is truly fearful and trembling; I bow before Your Majesty the Emperor, who has succeeded the enterprise of Yao and Shun and deployed armies like those of Tang of Shang and King Wu, pacifying the realm, cutting down the violent and rebellious, gathering distant peoples by sea and land, and uniting writing and cart-tracks.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject Yan prostrates himself in fear and trembling before Your Majesty, who has inherited the work of Yao and Shun, marshaled armies like Tang of Shang and King Wu, pacified the realm, crushed the wicked, gathered distant peoples by land and sea, and united the empire under one order.

sentences.zh: 臣方議改圖，便期納款，遽聞王師致討，實抱驚危。

translations.literal: Your subject was just discussing changing course and expected soon to offer submission, when I suddenly heard that the imperial army had come to punish me, and I am truly filled with alarm and peril.
translations.idiomatic: I was just preparing to change course and submit when I suddenly heard that the imperial army had come against me, and I am filled with alarm.

sentences.zh: 今則將千里之封疆，盡為王土；

translations.literal: Now a thousand li of territory shall all become imperial soil;
translations.idiomatic: Now a thousand li of territory shall all become imperial soil;

sentences.zh: 冀萬家之臣妾，皆沭皇恩。

translations.literal: I hope that the households and subjects of ten thousand families may all bathe in imperial grace.
translations.idiomatic: and I pray that every household among my people may bathe in imperial grace.

sentences.zh: 必當輿櫬乞降，負荊請命。

translations.literal: I shall surely come with my coffin to beg surrender and bear thorns to request judgment.
translations.idiomatic: I shall come with my coffin to beg surrender and bear thorns to ask for your judgment.

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇帝陛下，回照臨之造，施覆幬之仁，別示哀矜，以安反側。

translations.literal: I bow before Your Majesty the Emperor to turn back the grace of your oversight, extend the benevolence of your covering canopy, and show separate compassion to settle those who waver.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to turn back the grace of your oversight, extend the shelter of your mercy, and show special compassion to calm those who waver.

sentences.zh: 儻墳塋而獲祀，實存沒以知歸，臣無任望恩虔禱之至。

translations.literal: If my ancestral tombs may receive sacrifice, it will truly let the living and dead know where they belong; your subject is without limit in hoping for grace and in earnest prayer.
translations.idiomatic: If my ancestral tombs may still receive sacrifice, the living and dead alike will know where they belong. Your subject bows in boundless hope and earnest prayer.

sentences.zh: 乙酉年十一月日，臣王衍上表。

translations.literal: On a day of the eleventh month of the yiyou year, your subject Wang Yan submitted this memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Memorial submitted on a day in the eleventh month of the yiyou year by your subject Wang Yan.

sentences.zh: 」其月二十七日，魏王至成都北五里升仙橋，偽百官班於橋下，衍乘行輿至，素衣白馬，牽羊，草索系首，面縛銜璧，輿櫬於後。

translations.literal: On the twenty-seventh day of that month the Prince of Wei reached Shengxian Bridge five li north of Chengdu; the usurper officials formed ranks below the bridge; Yan came in a traveling carriage, in plain white garments on a white horse, leading a sheep, with a grass rope binding his head, his face bound and holding a jade disc in his mouth, with a coffin carried behind.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh the Prince of Wei reached Shengxian Bridge five li north of Chengdu. The Shu officials lined up below the bridge as Yan arrived in a traveling carriage, dressed in plain white on a white horse, leading a sheep, with a grass rope about his neck, his face bound and a jade disc in his mouth, and a coffin borne behind him.

sentences.zh: 魏王下馬受其璧，崇韜釋其縛，及燔其櫬，衍率偽百官東北舞蹈謝恩。

translations.literal: The Prince of Wei dismounted to receive the disc; Chongtao released his bonds and burned the coffin; Yan led the usurper officials in dancing toward the northeast to give thanks for grace.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Wei dismounted to accept the disc. Chongtao freed him and burned the coffin. Yan led the Shu officials in the surrender dance toward the northeast to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，拜，魏王、崇韜、李嚴皆答拜。

translations.literal: When the rites were finished they bowed; the Prince of Wei, Chongtao, and Li Yan all returned the bow.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished they bowed, and the Prince of Wei, Chongtao, and Li Yan bowed in return.

sentences.zh: 二十八日，王師入成都。

translations.literal: On the twenty-eighth day the imperial army entered Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-eighth the imperial army entered Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 自起師至入蜀城，凡七十五日。

translations.literal: From the raising of the army to entry into the Shu capital, altogether seventy-five days.
translations.idiomatic: From the opening of the campaign to the entry into the Shu capital, seventy-five days had passed.

sentences.zh: （案：以下原本殘闕。

translations.literal: (Note: Below this point the original text is defective.
translations.idiomatic: (Note: The original text below this point is defective.

sentences.zh: 據《歐陽史》云：同光四年，衍行至秦川驛，莊宗用伶人景進計，遣宦者向延嗣誅其族。

translations.literal: According to the Ouyang History: in the fourth year of Tongguang, as Yan traveled to Qinchuan Post, Zhuangzong followed the actor Jing Jin's plan and sent the eunuch Xiang Yansi to execute his clan.
translations.idiomatic: According to Ouyang Xiu's history, in Tongguang year 4, as Yan traveled to Qinchuan Post, Zhuangzong followed the actor Jing Jin's counsel and sent the eunuch Xiang Yansi to execute his entire clan.

sentences.zh: 天成二年，封衍順正公，以諸侯葬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng he was enfeoffed as Duke of Shunzheng and buried with the rites due a feudal lord.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancheng year 2 he was enfeoffed as Duke of Shunzheng and buried with the rites due a feudal lord.

sentences.zh: 《五代史補》：王建在許下時，尤不逞，嘗坐事遭徒，但無杖痕爾。

translations.literal: Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: When Wang Jian was at Xuchang he was especially unruly and once suffered banishment for an offense, but bore no marks of the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: When Wang Jian was at Xuchang he was notoriously unruly and once suffered banishment for an offense, yet bore no marks of beating.

sentences.zh: 及據蜀，得馬涓為從事，涓好詆訐，建恐為所譏，因問曰：「竊聞外議，以吾曾遭徒刑，有之乎！

translations.literal: When he held Shu he took Ma Juan as an aide; Juan loved to slander others, and Jian feared he would be mocked, so he asked, "I have heard in private talk outside that I once suffered penal servitude—is it so?"
translations.idiomatic: After he seized Shu he took Ma Juan as an aide. Juan loved to criticize others, and Jian feared mockery, so he asked, "I hear people say I once suffered penal servitude—is that true?"

sentences.zh: 」涓對曰：「有之。

translations.literal: Juan answered, "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: Juan answered, "It is true."

sentences.zh: 」建恃無杖痕，且對眾，因袒背以示涓曰：「請足下試看，有遭杖責而肌肉如是耶！

translations.literal: Jian relied on having no staff marks and, before the assembly, bared his back to show Juan, saying, "Please, sir, examine it—could one who suffered beating have flesh like this?"
translations.idiomatic: Confident that he bore no marks of beating, Jian bared his back before the assembly and said to Juan, "Look for yourself—could a man who had been beaten have flesh like this?"

sentences.zh: 」涓知其詐，乃撫背而嘆曰：「大奇，當時何處得此好膏藥來。

translations.literal: Juan knew it was a fraud and, stroking his back, sighed, "Most remarkable—where did you get such fine salve at the time?"
translations.idiomatic: Juan saw through the deception, stroked his back, and sighed, "Remarkable—where did you find salve that good?"

sentences.zh: 」賓佐皆失色，而涓晏然。

translations.literal: The guests all changed color, but Juan remained at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The guests turned pale, but Juan remained perfectly calm.

sentences.zh: 王建之僭號也，惟翰林學士最承恩顧，侍臣或諫其禮過，建曰：「蓋汝輩未之見也。

translations.literal: When Wang Jian assumed the imperial title, only the Hanlin academicians received the greatest favor; attendants sometimes remonstrated that the courtesy was excessive; Jian said, "That is because you have not seen it before.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jian took the imperial title, the Hanlin academicians alone enjoyed his greatest favor. Some attendants said the courtesy was excessive. Jian replied, "That is only because you have never seen how it was done before.

sentences.zh: 且吾在神策軍時，主內門魚鑰，見唐朝諸帝待翰林學士，雖交友不若也。

translations.literal: Moreover, when I was in the Shence Army and held the fish-keys of the inner gates, I saw how the Tang emperors treated Hanlin academicians—even close friends were not treated so well.
translations.idiomatic: When I was in the Shence Army and held the keys to the inner gates, I saw how Tang emperors treated their Hanlin academicians—even intimate friends were not honored so highly.

sentences.zh: 今我恩顧，比當時才有百分之一爾，何謂之過當耶！

translations.literal: The favor I now show is only one hundredth part of that time—how can you call it excessive!"
translations.idiomatic: What I show them now is only one hundredth part of that—how can you call it excessive?"

sentences.zh: 」論者多之。

translations.literal: Many commentators approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: Many commentators approved.

sentences.zh: 杜光庭，長安人，應《九經》舉不第。

translations.literal: Du Guangting was a native of Chang'an and failed the Nine Classics examination.
translations.idiomatic: Du Guangting came from Chang'an and failed the examination in the Nine Classics.

sentences.zh: 時長安有潘尊師者，道術甚高，僖宗所重，光庭素所希慕，數遊其門。

translations.literal: At that time in Chang'an there was Master Pan Zunshi, whose Daoist arts were very lofty and whom Emperor Xizong esteemed; Guangting had long admired him and often visited his gate.
translations.idiomatic: In Chang'an at the time lived Master Pan Zunshi, a Daoist of great renown whom Emperor Xizong favored. Guangting had long admired him and often visited his house.

sentences.zh: 當僖宗之幸蜀也，觀蜀中道門牢落，思得名士以主張之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong went to Shu, he observed that the Daoist community in Shu was desolate and wished to obtain a man of renown to lead it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong fled to Shu, he saw how depleted the Daoist community there was and wished to find a worthy man to restore it.

sentences.zh: 駕回，詔潘尊師使於兩街，求其可者，尊師奏曰：「臣觀兩街之眾，道聽途說，一時之俊即有之，至於掌教之士，恐未合應聖旨。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned, an edict sent Master Pan Zunshi as envoy to the two quarters to seek a suitable man; the master memorialized, saying, "Your subject has observed the crowds of the two quarters—there are men who hear the Way along the road and momentary talents may be found, but as for one to direct teaching, I fear none may answer the holy edict.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor returned, he sent Master Pan to search the two quarters of the capital for a suitable teacher. Pan memorialized, "I have looked through both quarters. Men who chatter about the Way are easy to find, but none who can truly lead teaching seems fit for Your Majesty's purpose.

sentences.zh: 臣於科場中識《九經》杜光庭，其人性簡而氣清，量寬而識遠，且困於風塵，思欲脫屣名利久矣，以臣愚思之，非光庭不可。

translations.literal: Your subject knew Du Guangting of the Nine Classics in the examination halls; his nature is simple and his spirit clear, his breadth great and his insight far, and he has long been weary of the dust of the world and wished to cast off fame and profit; in your subject's foolish judgment, none but Guangting will do.
translations.idiomatic: I know Du Guangting of the Nine Classics from the examination halls. His nature is plain and his spirit clear, his breadth great and his vision far. Long wearied by the world's turmoil, he has wished to cast off fame and profit. In my judgment, none but Guangting will do.

sentences.zh: 」僖宗詔而問之，一見大悅，遂令披戴，仍賜紫衣，號曰廣成先生，即日馳驛遣之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong summoned and questioned him; at first sight he was greatly pleased, ordered him to don the Daoist robes, also bestowed purple garments, styled him Master Guangcheng, and that same day sent him post-haste.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong summoned him and, delighted at first sight, had him take the Daoist robes, bestowed purple garments, styled him Master Guangcheng, and sent him to Shu that same day by urgent dispatch.

sentences.zh: 及王建據蜀，待之愈厚，又號為天師。

translations.literal: When Wang Jian held Shu he treated him all the more generously and also styled him Celestial Master.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jian held Shu he treated him even more generously and also styled him Celestial Master.

sentences.zh: 光庭嘗以《道》、《德》二經註者雖多，皆未能演暢其旨，因著《廣成義》八十卷，他術稱是，識者多之。）〉

translations.literal: Guangting once remarked that although commentaries on the Dao and De chapters were many, none could fully unfold their meaning; he therefore composed the Guangcheng Yi in eighty scrolls, and his other arts were likewise esteemed by those who knew him.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Guangting once said that although many had commented on the Dao and De chapters, none had truly unfolded their meaning, so he wrote the Guangcheng Yi in eighty scrolls. His other arts won equal praise from those who knew him.)]

sentences.zh: 孟知祥，字保裔，邢州龍岡人也。

translations.literal: Meng Zhixiang, style name Baoyi, was a native of Longgang in Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang, style name Baoyi, came from Longgang in Xing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖察，父道，世為郡校。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Cha, his father Dao; for generations they had been prefectural commandants.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Cha and his father Dao; for generations the family had served as prefectural commandants.

sentences.zh: 伯父方立，終於邢洺節度使，從父遷，位至澤潞節度使。

translations.literal: His father's elder brother Fangli ended as military governor of Xing-Mo; his father's younger brother Qian rose to military governor of Ze-Lu.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Fangli became military governor of Xing-Mo, and his uncle Qian rose to military governor of Ze-Lu.

sentences.zh: 知祥在後唐莊宗同光三年，授西川節度副大使，知節度事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongguang under Later Tang Emperor Zhuangzong, Zhixiang was appointed deputy military governor of Xichuan with authority over military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Tang Tongguang year 3, Zhuangzong appointed Zhixiang deputy military governor of Xichuan with full authority over the circuit.

sentences.zh: 天成中，安重誨專權用事，以知祥莊宗舊識，方據大藩，慮久而難制，潛欲圖之。

translations.literal: In the Tiancheng era An Chonghui monopolized power; because Zhixiang was an old acquaintance of Zhuangzong and now held a great frontier post, he feared that in time he would be hard to control and secretly wished to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiancheng era An Chonghui monopolized power. Zhixiang was an old acquaintance of Zhuangzong and now held a great frontier post, and An feared that in time he would prove hard to control and secretly plotted against him.

sentences.zh: 是時，客省使李嚴以嘗使於蜀，洞知其利柄，因獻謀於重誨，請以己為西川監軍，庶效方略，以制知祥，朝廷可之。

translations.literal: At that time the guest-bureau envoy Li Yan, because he had once been envoy to Shu and thoroughly knew its leverage, therefore offered a plan to Chonghui, asking to be made supervising commissioner for Xichuan so that he might put strategies into effect to control Zhixiang; the court approved.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the guest-bureau envoy Li Yan, who had once served in Shu and knew its leverage points well, offered Chonghui a plan to make himself supervising commissioner for Xichuan so he could restrain Zhixiang. The court approved.

sentences.zh: 及嚴至蜀，知祥延接甚至，徐謂嚴曰：「都監前因奉使，請兵伐蜀，遂使東、西兩川俱至破滅，川中之人，其怨已深。

translations.literal: When Yan reached Shu, Zhixiang received him with the utmost courtesy and slowly said to Yan, "Supervising Commissioner, on your former mission you requested troops to campaign against Shu, and thereby brought both eastern and western Chuan to ruin; the people of the Chuan region bear deep resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan reached Shu, Zhixiang received him with elaborate courtesy and then said slowly, "Supervising Commissioner, on your last mission you asked for troops to conquer Shu and brought both Chuan circuits to ruin. The people of Shu bear you a deep grudge.

sentences.zh: 今既復來，人情大駭，固奉為不暇也。」

translations.literal: Now that you have come again, popular feeling is greatly alarmed, and I truly have no leisure to receive you."
translations.idiomatic: Now that you have come again, the people are terrified, and I truly have no leisure to receive you."

sentences.zh: （案：此句疑有舛誤。）〉

translations.literal: (Note: This sentence is suspected to be corrupt.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Note: This sentence is suspected to be corrupt.)]

sentences.zh: 即遣人拽下階，斬於階前。

translations.literal: He immediately sent men to drag him down the steps and behead him before the steps.
translations.idiomatic: He at once had men drag Yan down the steps and behead him on the spot.

sentences.zh: （《歐陽史》云：李嚴至境上，遣人持書候知祥，知祥盛兵見之，冀嚴懼而不來，嚴聞之自若。

translations.literal: (The Ouyang History says: When Li Yan reached the border he sent a man with a letter to greet Zhixiang; Zhixiang displayed his army in strength to receive him, hoping Yan would be afraid and not come; when Yan heard of it he remained composed.
translations.idiomatic: (Ouyang Xiu's history says that when Li Yan reached the border he sent a letter ahead. Zhixiang displayed a large army, hoping Yan would be frightened and turn back, but Yan remained composed.

sentences.zh: 天成二年正月，嚴至成都，知祥置酒召嚴，因責嚴曰：「今諸方鎮已罷監軍，公何得來？

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Tiancheng Yan reached Chengdu; Zhixiang set out wine and summoned Yan, then reproached him, saying, "Now all the military governors have abolished supervising commissioners—how dare you come?"
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Tiancheng year 2 Yan reached Chengdu. Zhixiang gave a banquet and summoned him, then rebuked him: "Every other province has abolished supervising commissioners—how dare you come?"

sentences.zh: 」《鑒戒錄》云：李嚴於天成初復來臨護，孟祖加之禮分，從容數其五罪，命劍斬之。

translations.literal: The Jianjie Lu says: When Li Yan came again early in Tiancheng to supervise, the Meng founder treated him with courtesy, calmly enumerated his five crimes, and ordered him cut down with the sword.
translations.idiomatic: The Jianjie Lu says that when Li Yan returned early in Tiancheng, the Meng founder received him courteously, calmly listed five crimes against him, and ordered him cut down with the sword.

sentences.zh: 與《薛史》異。）〉

translations.literal: This differs from the Xue History.)〉
translations.idiomatic: This differs from the Xue History.)]

sentences.zh: 其後朝廷每除劍南牧守，皆令提兵而往，或千或百，分守郡城。

translations.literal: Afterward, whenever the court appointed a Jiannan prefect or administrator, it ordered him to lead troops thither, sometimes a thousand or a hundred, to garrison the prefectural cities separately.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter whenever the court appointed a Jiannan prefect or administrator, it sent him with troops—sometimes a thousand, sometimes a hundred—to garrison the prefectural cities.

sentences.zh: 時董璋作鎮東川已數年矣，亦有雄據之意。

translations.literal: At that time Dong Zhang had governed Dongchuan for several years and also cherished the ambition of holding territory by force.
translations.idiomatic: By then Dong Zhang had governed Dongchuan for several years and harbored ambitions of his own.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷以夏魯奇鎮遂州，李仁矩鎮閬州，皆領兵數千人赴鎮，復授以密旨，令制禦兩川。

translations.literal: It happened that the court stationed Xia Luqi at Sui Prefecture and Li Renju at Lang Prefecture, each leading several thousand troops to their posts, and further gave them secret instructions to restrain the two Chuan circuits.
translations.idiomatic: The court then stationed Xia Luqi at Sui Prefecture and Li Renju at Lang Prefecture, each with several thousand troops, and gave them secret orders to restrain both Chuan circuits.

sentences.zh: 董璋覺之，乃與知祥通好，結為婚家，以固輔車之勢。

translations.literal: Dong Zhang perceived this and therefore entered into friendly relations with Zhixiang, becoming affines by marriage to strengthen their mutual support like paired wheels.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang saw what was happening and made peace with Zhixiang, sealing the bond with marriage so the two domains would stand or fall together.

sentences.zh: 知祥慮唐軍驟至，與遂、閬兵合，則勢不可支吾，遂與璋協謀，令璋以本部軍先取閬州，知祥遣大將軍李仁罕、趙廷隱率軍圍遂州。

translations.literal: Zhixiang feared that if Tang troops arrived suddenly and joined with the forces of Sui and Lang he could not hold out; he therefore plotted with Zhang, ordering Zhang to take Lang Prefecture first with his own troops while Zhixiang sent the great generals Li Renhan and Zhao Tingyin to lead an army and besiege Sui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang feared that if Tang troops arrived suddenly and joined the garrisons at Sui and Lang he could not hold out. He plotted with Zhang: Zhang would seize Lang Prefecture first with his own army while Zhixiang sent Li Renhan and Zhao Tingyin to besiege Sui.

sentences.zh: 長興元年冬，唐軍伐蜀，至劍門。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Changxing the Tang army campaigned against Shu and reached Jianmen.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Changxing year 1 the Tang army marched against Shu and reached Jianmen Pass.

sentences.zh: 二年，以遂、閬既陷，又糧運不接，乃班師。

translations.literal: In the second year, because Sui and Lang had already fallen and grain transport could not connect, the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, with Sui and Lang already fallen and supplies cut off, the Tang army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 三年，知祥又破董璋，乃自領東、西兩川節度使。

translations.literal: In the third year Zhixiang again defeated Dong Zhang and thereupon personally took command as military governor of both eastern and western Chuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Zhixiang defeated Dong Zhang again and took command of both Chuan circuits himself.

sentences.zh: 應順元年，以劍南東兩川節度使、王稱我帝於蜀，改元明德。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yingshun, as military governor of the eastern and western circuits of Jiannan, he styled himself emperor in Shu and changed the era name to Mingde.
translations.idiomatic: In Yingshun year 1, as military governor of both Jiannan circuits, he declared himself emperor in Shu and proclaimed the Mingde era.

sentences.zh: 七月卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: He died in the seventh month at the age of sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh month at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: （案：《孟知祥傳》，《永樂大典》原闕，今采《冊府元龜》僭偽部以存梗概。）〉

translations.literal: (Note: The biography of Meng Zhixiang was originally missing in the Yongle Dadian; the present text is taken from the section on usurpers in the Cefu Yuangui to preserve the outline.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Note: The biography of Meng Zhixiang was missing from the Yongle Dadian. The outline here is drawn from the usurpers section of the Cefu Yuangui.)]

sentences.zh: 昶，知祥之第三子也。

translations.literal: Chang was Zhixiang's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was Zhixiang's third son.

sentences.zh: （《宋朝事實》云：昶，初名仁贊。

translations.literal: (Facts of the Song Dynasty says: Chang's original name was Renzan.
translations.idiomatic: (Facts of the Song Dynasty says Chang's original name was Renzan.

sentences.zh: 《揮麈餘話》云：昶，字保元。）〉

translations.literal: Remaining Tales from the Whisk says: Chang's style name was Baoyuan.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Remaining Tales from the Whisk says his style name was Baoyuan.)]

sentences.zh: 母李氏，本莊宗之嬪御，以賜知祥。

translations.literal: His mother was Lady Li, originally a consort of Zhuangzong, who was given to Zhixiang.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Li had been a consort of Zhuangzong before she was given to Zhixiang.

sentences.zh: 唐天祐十六年，歲在己卯，十一月十四日，生昶於太原。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Tianyou of Tang, the year jimao, on the fourteenth day of the eleventh month, Chang was born at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang Tianyou year 16, the jimao year, on the fourteenth day of the eleventh month, Chang was born at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 及知祥鎮蜀，昶與其母從知祥妻瓊華長公主同入於蜀。

translations.literal: When Zhixiang governed Shu, Chang and his mother followed Zhixiang's wife, the Princess of Qionghua, into Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhixiang took command in Shu, Chang and his mother followed Zhixiang's wife, Princess Qionghua, into the province.

sentences.zh: 知祥僭號，偽冊為皇太子。

translations.literal: When Zhixiang assumed the imperial title, he was enfeoffed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhixiang took the imperial title, Chang was named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 知祥卒，遂襲其偽位，時年十六，尚稱明德元年。

translations.literal: When Zhixiang died, he succeeded to the usurper's throne at the age of sixteen, still calling it the first year of Mingde.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhixiang died, Chang succeeded him at sixteen, still calling the year Mingde 1.

sentences.zh: 及偽明德四年冬，偽詔改明年為廣政元年，是歲即晉天福三年也。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year of the usurper era Mingde, a usurper edict changed the following year to the first year of Guangzheng; that year was the third year of Tianfu of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Mingde year 4 an edict renamed the coming year Guangzheng 1, which corresponded to Later Jin Tianfu year 3.

sentences.zh: 偽廣政十三年，偽上尊號為睿文英武仁聖明孝皇帝。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of the usurper era Guangzheng he was given the exalted title Emperor of Sagely Culture, Martial Brilliance, Humaneness, Sagacity, and Filial Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangzheng year 13 he took the exalted title Emperor of Sagely Culture, Martial Brilliance, Humaneness, Sagacity, and Filial Brightness.

sentences.zh: 皇朝乾德三年春，王師平蜀，詔昶舉族赴闕，賜甲第於京師，迨其臣下賜賫甚厚，尋冊封楚王。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year of Qiande of the imperial dynasty the imperial army pacified Shu; an edict ordered Chang and his whole clan to come to court; a fine mansion in the capital was bestowed; his subordinates were richly rewarded; soon he was enfeoffed as King of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of imperial Qiande year 3 the imperial army pacified Shu. Chang and his clan were ordered to court, given a fine mansion in the capital, and his followers richly rewarded. Soon he was enfeoffed as King of Chu.

sentences.zh: 是歲秋，卒於東京，時年四十七，事具皇家日曆。

translations.literal: That autumn he died in the Eastern Capital at the age of forty-seven; the full account is in the imperial calendar.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he died in the Eastern Capital at forty-seven; the full account appears in the imperial calendar.

sentences.zh: 自知祥同光二年丙戌歲入蜀，父子相繼，凡四十年而亡。

translations.literal: From the time Zhixiang entered Shu in the bingxu year, the second year of Tongguang, father and son succeeded one another for forty years in all before perishing.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhixiang's entry into Shu in Tongguang year 2, the bingxu year, father and son ruled in succession for forty years before the realm fell.

sentences.zh: （《五代史補》：孟知祥之入蜀，視其險固，陰有割據之志。

translations.literal: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: When Meng Zhixiang entered Shu he observed its rugged security and secretly cherished the ambition of carving out a domain.
translations.idiomatic: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: When Meng Zhixiang entered Shu he saw how rugged and secure it was and secretly resolved to carve out a domain of his own.

sentences.zh: 洎抵成都，值晚，且憩於郊外。

translations.literal: When he reached Chengdu it was already late, and he rested for a time in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Chengdu it was already evening, and he rested awhile in the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 有推小車子過者，其物皆以袋盛，知祥見，問曰：「汝車所勝幾袋？

translations.literal: A man pushing a small cart passed by; his goods were all packed in bags; Zhixiang saw him and asked, "How many bags can your cart bear at most?"
translations.idiomatic: A man pushing a small cart passed by, his goods all packed in bags. Zhixiang asked, "How many bags can your cart hold at most?"

sentences.zh: 」推者曰：「極力不過兩袋。

translations.literal: The pusher said, "With full effort no more than two bags."
translations.idiomatic: The man answered, "At most two bags, even with all my strength."

sentences.zh: 」知祥惡之，後果兩代而亡。

translations.literal: Zhixiang disliked this, and in the end the realm indeed perished after two generations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang took this as an ill omen, and in the end the realm fell after only two generations.

sentences.zh: 知祥與董璋有隙，舉兵討之。

translations.literal: Zhixiang had a breach with Dong Zhang and raised troops to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang fell out with Dong Zhang and marched against him.

sentences.zh: 璋素勇悍，聞知祥之來也，以為送死。

translations.literal: Zhang had always been brave and fierce; hearing that Zhixiang was coming, he thought Zhixiang was coming to deliver himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang had always been fierce in battle and, hearing that Zhixiang was coming, assumed he was marching to his own destruction.

sentences.zh: 諸將兩端，李鎬為知祥判官，深憂之。

translations.literal: The generals wavered between two sides; Li Gao served as Zhixiang's aide and was deeply worried.
translations.idiomatic: The generals wavered, and Li Gao, Zhixiang's aide, was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 及將戰，知祥欲示閑暇，自寫一書以遺董璋。

translations.literal: As battle was about to begin, Zhixiang wished to show ease and personally wrote a letter to send to Dong Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of battle Zhixiang wished to appear at ease and personally wrote a letter to Dong Zhang.

sentences.zh: 無何，舉筆輒誤書「董」為「重」字，不悅久之。

translations.literal: Before long, whenever he raised the brush he mistakenly wrote the character for Dong as the character for heavy, and was displeased for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he found that whenever he lifted the brush he wrote Dong's name as the character for "heavy" instead, and he brooded over it for a long time.

sentences.zh: 鎬在側大喜，且引諸將賀於馬前，知祥不測，曰：「事未可測，何賀耶！

translations.literal: Gao at his side was greatly pleased and led the generals to congratulate him before his horse; Zhixiang could not fathom it and said, "The outcome cannot yet be known—why congratulate?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao beside him was delighted and led the generals to congratulate him before his horse. Zhixiang was baffled and said, "The outcome is not yet known—why congratulate me?"

sentences.zh: 」鎬曰：「其『董』字『艹』下施『重』。

translations.literal: Gao said, "In the character for Dong, below the grass radical is placed the character for heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Gao said, "In the character Dong, the grass radical sits above the character for heavy.

sentences.zh: 今大王去『艹』書『重』是『董』已無頭，此必勝之兆也。

translations.literal: Now Your Highness has removed the grass and written heavy—this means Dong has lost his head; it is surely an omen of victory."
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness has removed the grass and written only heavy—Dong has lost his head. This is surely an omen of victory."

sentences.zh: 」於是三軍欣然，一戰而董璋敗。）〉

translations.literal: Thereupon the three armies were pleased, and in one battle Dong Zhang was defeated.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The whole army took heart, and in a single battle Dong Zhang was defeated.)]

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：昔張孟陽為《劍閣銘》云：「惟蜀之門，作固作鎮，世濁則逆，道清斯順。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Long ago Zhang Mengyang wrote in the Inscription on Jiange, saying, "Only the gate of Shu serves as fortress and barrier; when the age is turbid it turns rebellious, when the Way is clear it submits.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer remarks: Long ago Zhang Mengyang wrote in the Inscription on Jiange Pass, "Shu alone is the empire's gate, its fortress and its barrier: in turbid ages it turns rebellious, in ages of clear governance it submits.

sentences.zh: 」是知自古坤維之地，遇亂代則閉之而不通，逢興運則取之如俯拾。

translations.literal: From this one knows that from antiquity the land of the southwest corner, when it met a chaotic age, was shut and not passed through; when it encountered a flourishing fortune, was taken as if picking up objects from the ground.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that from antiquity the southwest has been closed off in ages of disorder and seized with ease whenever fortune smiled on the throne.

sentences.zh: 然唐氏之入蜀也，兵力雖勝，帝道猶昏，故數年間得之復失。

translations.literal: Yet when the house of Tang entered Shu, although military strength prevailed, the imperial Way was still benighted, and therefore within a few years what was gained was lost again.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the Tang entered Shu, though their armies prevailed, the imperial Way was still clouded, and within a few years what they gained they lost again.

sentences.zh: 及皇上之平蜀也，煦之以堯日，和之以舜風，故比戶之民，悅而從化。

translations.literal: When the present emperor pacified Shu, he warmed it with the sun of Yao and harmonized it with the wind of Shun, and therefore the people household by household rejoiced and submitted to transformation.
translations.idiomatic: When the present emperor pacified Shu, he warmed it with Yao's sun and harmonized it with Shun's wind, so that household after household rejoiced and submitted.

sentences.zh: 且夫王衍之遭季世也，則赤族於秦川；

translations.literal: Moreover, when Wang Yan encountered a degenerate age, his whole clan was exterminated in the Qinchuan region;
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yan met a degenerate age, his entire clan was exterminated in the Qinchuan region;

sentences.zh: 孟昶之遇明代也，則受封於楚甸。

translations.literal: when Meng Chang encountered a bright age, he received enfeoffment in the Chu region.
translations.idiomatic: but when Meng Chang met a bright age, he received enfeoffment in the Chu region.

sentences.zh: 雖俱為亡國之主，何幸與不幸相去之遠也！

translations.literal: Although both were lords of perished states, how far apart their fortune and misfortune were!
translations.idiomatic: Though both were rulers of fallen realms, how vast was the distance between their fortune and their ruin!
